chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah, Exalted is He, support him—reported to me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a person in janabah sitting in the mosques. He said: “No; rather, he may pass through all of them except al-Masjid al-Haram and the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الرَّسُولِ: the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله in Madinah

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah sit in or pass through a mosque according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the person in a state of janabah and their relation to mosques. It states that such a person may not sit in mosques, though passing through them is allowed, except for al-Masjid al-Haram and the Mosque of the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.
